traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and technical requirements in docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md are implemented and verified by passing tests.
Mapping to requirements: - REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE and REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION are covered by valid/invalid @supports tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts (including missing values, missing IDs, invalid story paths, and invalid requirement IDs), all passing. - REQ-SUPPORTS-VALIDATE, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, and REQ-SCOPED-IDS are covered by multi-story @supports cases in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts, which validate that each requirement is checked against its story file, that errors mention the story path, and that the same requirement ID can appear in multiple stories without conflict. - REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-SUPPORTS is exercised for story enforcement in tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts and for requirement enforcement in tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts, both treating @supports-alone annotations as valid while still flagging plain unannotated functions. - REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT is validated by numerous tests that confirm legacy @story/@req behavior (valid and error cases) remains unchanged, including explicit BACKCOMPAT-named tests. - REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT is directly tested by a passing mixed-usage case in valid-annotation-format.test.ts and by the co-existence of both styles across the rule tests. - Quality Standards are supported by the broader ESLint rule configuration and plugin tests (config schemas, presets, plugin export tests) all passing, indicating the @supports-related changes align with existing ESLint best practices. - Documentation acceptance criteria are satisfied by the story’s own examples and migration section.
Given the story file contents match the specification, all relevant tests referencing this story pass, and they explicitly cover each behavioral requirement, the story is fully implemented and verified.
